title: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 — Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions (challenge statement)
notes: Challenge requirements (five hazards; blood pressure, heart rate, blood glucose, body temperature, sleep duration, mood) were taken from the challenge text supplied to the team. The 2026 event page was confirmed to exist; the individual challenge page was not retrieved by the build agent.

title: Human Research Program — The Five Hazards of Human Spaceflight
notes: Defines the five hazards: space radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, gravity fields, hostile/closed environments; states that the hazards do not stand alone.

title: Human Research Program — Risks of Human Spaceflight
notes: Lists HRP risks including altered immune response, reduced cardiorespiratory and musculoskeletal fitness, SANS, bone changes, behavioral conditions, inadequate sleep and irregular schedules, radiation-induced cancers, host-microorganism interactions, cardiovascular adaptations.

title: Human System Risks (Human System Risk Board risk list)
publisher: NASA Office of the Chief Health & Medical Officer
notes: Formal risk titles, e.g. Risk of Bone Fracture due to Spaceflight-induced Changes to Bone; Risk of Renal Stone Formation; Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome; Risk of Altered Sensorimotor/Vestibular Function; Risk of Performance Decrements and Adverse Health Outcomes Resulting from Sleep Loss, Circadian Desynchronization, and Work Overload; Risk of Toxic Exposure; Risk of Adverse Health Event Due To Altered Immune Response.

title: Human Health and Performance: Keeping Astronauts Safe & Productive On a Mission to Mars
notes: Maps the five hazards to human system risks; hazards are coupled; radiation monitoring/notification onboard; increasing crew independence from mission control with distance.

title: Human System Risk at NASA (Antonsen, 2019)
notes: Hazard-to-risk mapping: distance → autonomous medical care capacity; isolation → behavioral, sleep, team dynamics; hostile/closed → CO2, toxic exposures, water, food, decreased immune function.

title: Human Research Program overview (Platts, 2023)
notes: Risk posture tables by mission type for bone fracture, renal stone formation, SANS, sensorimotor alterations, cardiovascular adaptations, behavioral conditions.

title: NASA-STD-3001 Volume 1 Revision C — NASA Spaceflight Human-System Standard: Crew Health
publisher: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer
notes: [V1 3003] in-mission preventive health care incl. monitoring of physiological and psychosocial well-being; [V1 3004] in-mission medical care incl. private two-way communication; [V1 4011] mission cognitive status; [V1 4014] completion of critical tasks (planned sleep period limits); [V1 4029] ALARA; [V1 4030] career space permissible exposure limit; [V1 6001] circadian shifting operations and fatigue management — rationale recommends an 8.5-hour sleep period in crew schedule planning; [V1 6002] private medical communication (stored/forward allowed when delays exist).

title: OCHMO Technical Briefs (index) — derived from NASA-STD-3001 Volumes 1 and 2
publisher: NASA Office of the Chief Health & Medical Officer
notes: Index of technical briefs. Technical briefs state they are for reference only and do not supersede or waive Agency, Program or Contract requirements.

title: NASA-STD-3001 Technical Brief OCHMO-TB-041 Sleep Accommodations (Rev B, 2023-10-23)
notes: Sleep quantity and quality factors; average in-flight sleep of about six hours; cites [V1 6001] circadian shifting operations and fatigue management. Does not itself state the 8.5 h figure (that is in the V1 Rev C rationale).

title: NASA-STD-3001 Technical Brief OCHMO-TB-016 Behavioral Health and Performance (Rev B)
notes: Relevant requirements: [V1 6002] Private Medical Communication schedule, [V1 6004] Behavioral health and performance provisions, [V1 6010] Psychological communication schedule.

title: NASA-STD-3001 Technical Brief OCHMO-TB-004 Carbon Dioxide (CO2)
notes: NASA-STD-3001 Volume 2 Rev D [V2 6004] limits the average 1-hour CO2 partial pressure in the habitable volume to no more than 3 mmHg. Headaches on ISS associated with CO2 level; fluid shift produces similar symptoms. [V2 6001] trend analysis of environmental data.

title: Lowering CO2 exposure on the ISS: crew symptoms at lower levels than historically accepted
notes: Reports crew symptoms attributable to CO2 starting at 2.3 mmHg and wide inter- and intra-individual variability in CO2 sensitivity; CO2 symptoms asked about in weekly private medical conferences.

title: NASA-STD-3001 Technical Brief OCHMO-TB-003 Habitable Atmosphere
notes: Atmosphere hazards include inadequate oxygen supply (hypoxia or hyperoxia) and pressure changes; pressures expressed in mmHg, psia or kPa.

title: NASA-STD-3001 Technical Brief OCHMO-TB-002 ECLSS: Human-Centered Approach
notes: Environmental control: temperature, humidity, atmosphere, crew health environmental limits; related briefs on toxicology, water, bone loss.

title: NASA-STD-3001 Technical Brief OCHMO-TB-020 Design for Ionizing Radiation Protection
notes: Countermeasures: shielding, monitoring, accurate event determination, dosimetry and timely reporting to alert crew to seek shelter. Requirements include [V2 6161] intravehicular area monitoring and [V2 6162] personal monitoring of space radiation exposure, [V1 4029] ALARA.

title: Space Radiation (HRP hazard page) — Space Radiation Analysis Group monitoring and dosimetry
notes: SRAG provides continuous space radiation environment monitoring; crew dosimeters measure radiation; insufficient knowledge for long-duration exposure recommendations.

title: Space agency-specific standards for crew dose and risk assessment of ionising radiation exposures for the International Space Station
notes: Crew Active Dosimeters store and self-report time-resolved exposure; monitoring crew radiation exposure is essential and obligatory.

title: Evidence Report: Risk of Adverse Cognitive or Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders
notes: Approved for public release 2025-02-10. Covers behavioral health signs and symptoms, predictors and contributing factors, exploration-mission stressors.

title: Cardiovascular risks and hazards associated with deep space exploration
notes: Reviews cardiovascular adaptation, orthostatic changes after flight, sleep deprivation and circadian misalignment in astronauts (~6 h sleep per day reported).

title: ASTRA demonstration-only rule set (synthetic, not clinically validated)
notes: Statistical rules relative to an individual baseline used only to demonstrate the workflow. NOT NASA-approved. NOT clinical thresholds. Must be replaced by clinician-approved criteria before any operational use.
